- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is flat or trending down, adjust upward by 2–5% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.
- If recent auction supply events are frequent (≥15/30d) and model forecast is rising, cap upward momentum at 1–3% above recent peak to avoid overshoot.
- If true outcome spikes sharply after a flat forecast (e.g., 30d forecast = 65, true = 75+), apply a “lag correction” — add 1–3% to forecast for next 3–5 days to capture delayed reaction.
- When bullish events outnumber bearish (net bullish > 0), model tends to underpredict — increase forecast baseline by 1–3% to reflect policy-driven upside.
- If sentiment history shows repeated bearish swings (e.g., -0.33, -0.50) and forecast is rising, apply a “mean reversion” bias — reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1% per 3-day horizon to avoid overcorrection.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and net bearish supply, apply a “downward bias” — subtract 1–3% from forecast if recent sentiment is neutral or bearish.
- If model forecast is flat and true outcome shows strong upward trend (e.g., 70→75+), assume “sentiment lag” — forecast next 3–5 days should rise 1–2% per day to reflect delayed market reaction.
